subject: general
question: The mode and median of a dataset is 52.7 and 65, respectively. What is the mean of the dataset? (Use empirical formula, and round off your answer to one decimal place.)
solution: __Shortcut Trick__ Apply the **Empirical Formula**: **Mean = (3 × Median − Mode) ÷ 2**. Substitute the given values: **Mean = (3 × 65 − 52.7) ÷ 2**. **Mean = (195 − 52.7) ÷ 2 = 142.3 ÷ 2 = 71.15**. Rounding to one decimal place, we get **71.2**. **∴ The correct answer is 71.2.** **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** **Mode** = 52.7 and **Median** = 65. **Formula Used:** **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9c6435b5decb3f386276b8f9c1ecee96cb4dc2f9570c85aab79fab57c15c3399.png] ⇒ 52.7 = 3 × 65 − 2 × Mean ⇒ 52.7 = 195 − 2 × Mean ⇒ 2 × Mean = 195 − 52.7 ⇒ 2 × Mean = 142.3 ⇒ Mean = 142.3 ÷ 2 ⇒ Mean = 71.15 ≈ 71.2 **∴ The correct answer is 71.2.** **__Additional Information__** Empirical Relationship The relationship **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean** is an approximation used for **unimodal** and **moderately skewed** distributions.
